contexts.text: The men of the Most Ancient Church... were instructed by means of (most delicious and paradisiacal) visions and dreams. AC 597, Explained. (And there was insinuated into them what they signified. AC 1122.) AC 2179:3.
The visions of the prophets were... openings of their interior sight. Enumerated. AC 1619. AC 1626.
The external man... is then illuminated by the internal, and is then in the Divine vision here treated of... The Lord, when a boy, was, as to His external man, very often in such Divine sight...

Vision () = inmost revelation, which is that of perception. (For) visions are according to the man's state. A vision presented before those whose interiors have been closed, is very differently circumstanced from a vision which is presented before those whose interiors are open. Example(s).

There are many kinds of visions... The more interior the visions are, the more perfect they are. With the Lord they were the most perfect of all, because He had, at the time, a perception of all things in the World of Spirits and in the Heavens; and He had an immediate communication with Jehovah. This communication is represented... by the vision in which Jehovah appeared to Abraham.
Two extraordinary kinds of vision, called being withdrawn from the body, and being carried by the spirit to another place. Described. HH 440. HH 441.
But the things ordinarily seen (by Swedenborg) were not visions; but were things seen in the highest wakefulness of the body.
On visions and dreams, including the prophetical ones of the Word. General article.
Visions which are seen in phantasy, and which are illusions. Explained. SE 1752.
These persons are visionaries.
Enthusiastic Spirits... have visions about things to be believed. Explained.

By genuine visions are meant the visions or sights of the Things which really exist in the other life... and which appear to a man when his interior sight is opened by the Lord... Such were the visions of the prophets. Described.
The visions which take place before good Spirits, are representatives of the Things which are in Heaven. Explained... Such things are perpetual with good Spirits.
The visions, or rather sights, which appear before the eyes of the spirit... are more and more interior. Described.
The kinds of vision are too numerous to mention.
Two visions described by way of illustration. AC 1974. See also AC 1977.
(Representative) dreams inflow from Heaven: equally with visions, but with the difference that dreams do so when the body is asleep, and visions when it is not asleep.
A vision of Daniel Explained. AE 316:16. AE 594:3.
A vision = truths; here () falsities.
The valley of vision () = phantasies from sensuous things about spiritual things.
God said to Israel in the visions of the night () = an obscure revelation... For revelations took place either by dreams, by visions of the night, by visions of the day, or (in other ways).

I will turn aside and see this great vision () = reflection upon this revelation... A vision = revelation. It is called a great vision, because, in the supreme sense, by the flame in the bush is signified the Divine truth united to the Divine good in the Lord's Human.
A vision of vanity () = a false revelation.
By to see, or by a vision, when predicated of the prophets, is signified a revelation which regards doctrine; and by to divine is signified a revelation which regards life.
The prophetic visions of the Word. Explained.
(In the Sixth Earth) a Divine vision is distinguished from a vision which is not Divine (by the appearing of an Angel); for in a vision not Divine no Angel appears.
Such are visionaries and enthusiasts. Described.

As they wondered that this has not been manifested to man by means of visions... they were told from Heaven that it could have been done... but still (such) would not have believed; and besides that it is dangerous to confirm anything by visions with those who are in falsities, because they would first believe, and afterwards deny, and would thus profane the truth... TCR 282, Explained.
I asseverate that these things are not visions; but sights in complete wakefulness.
The sensation (which the Moravians feel) is from visionary Spirits.

We read of the prophets that they were in vision; and also that Jehovah spoke to them. When they were in vision, they were not in their bodies, but in their spirit, in which state they saw such things as there are in Heaven... In their state of vision the eyes of their spirits were opened, and the eyes of their bodies were closed; and they then also seemed to themselves to be carried from place to place, the body remaining in its own place. In this state were, sometimes, Ezekiel, Zechariah, Daniel, and John when he wrote the Apocalypse; and it is said, then, that they were in vision, or in the spirit. Illustrated. AR 36. AR 945:2.
That no one is reformed by means of visions... because they compel. Explained.

Visions are of two kinds: Divine, and diabolical. Divine visions are effected by means of the representatives in Heaven; but diabolical visions by means of the magical things which are in Hell. There are also fantastic visions, which are the deceptive mockeries of an abstracted mind. Divine visions are such as were those of the prophets, who, when in them, were not in the body, but in the spirit; for visions cannot appeal to any man in wakefulness of the body; and therefore when they appeared to the prophets it is said that they were in the spirit Illustrated.

Such were the visions which appeared from Heaven before the sight of their spirits, and not before that of their bodies. Such visions do not happen at this day, for if they did they would not be understood, because they are effected by means of representatives...

Diabolical visions, however, have sometimes happened, being induced by enthusiastic and visionary Spirits, who, from the delirium in which they were, called themselves the Holy Spirit. But these Spirits have now been collected together by the Lord, and cast into a Hell separate from the Hells of others.
The things which John saw were only visions... These see in John's visions arcana...
The spiritual state in which John was when in the visions. Signified.
But the Word was not revealed in a state of the spirit, that is, in vision...
The things which John saw were visions which were representative...
I saw the horses in the vision () = that... the reasonings... were imaginary and visionary. Explained. ( = the falsification of the understanding of the Word. AE 575.)
Their heads = imaginary and visionary things about faith alone, which are called phantasies.

What are faith in act, and faith in state... but visionary things?... What is the remission of sins and the consequent instantaneous Salvation but a thing of visionary thought? (Other examples of these visionary things of faith alone.)
All such are in posterior vision, and not in any prior sight.
The visionary concupiscence, or phantasy, of possessing all wealth. Described.

By being in the spirit... is meant a state of the mind in which it is separate from the body; and as, in this state, the prophets saw such things as come forth in the Spiritual World, it is called the vision of God. Explained and ill. This is the state in which I have been for twenty-six years, with this difference: that I have been in the spirit and at the same time in the body...
A visionary and absurd faith... is falsity appearing like truth from ingenious confirmation.
(Of the four kinds of spiritual sight) the second, is vision with the eyes closed. Described. SE 2951.
On visions which are illusions. General article. SE 1755.

Unless a man is in faith in the Lord, he may easily be led to believe that such (illusory) visions are from Heaven, when yet they are of the devil; for they cannot be distinguished from true visions... except by those who are led by the Lord. But at this day such things are forbidden...
I saw direful visions... but still even in this injected terror, I felt secure.
(A Spirit who could produce visions which gave delight; but he afterwards inflicted injury.)
A vision concerning the interiors of the Word. Described.
(This) was shown me by a vision. Described.
A representative vision about the Quakers. Described.
A vision about the more subtle magicians. Described.
Such were represented in a semi-waking nocturnal vision. Described.
(This) was not speech, but vision, accompanied with a manifest perception of the Thing.
On a vision of a house and the Spirits there, and also of a city and buildings. Described.
I was in a waking vision. Described. SE 4773. SE 4784.
Where there is enlightenment, there must also be a vision of the contraries.
I was in a nocturnal vision, or dream. Described.
This has been shown me in a vision of the night. Described.
They said to him that these things were visions, and not real. He replied that he knew they were visions, but as he saw them with his eyes, and felt the pain... it must be real.
(This) is perceived by interior vision.
The man supposes that (this) is an illusion, or vision. Described.

That they have completely deprived themselves of truths, and immersed themselves in falsities, is described by, They said to the seers. See not; and to those that have vision, See not for us right things, speak unto us smooth things; see illusions ().
The Intellectual of those of the Church... is enlightened when the Word is read; and therefore it is said... I will multiply vision (). Vision = the truths of doctrine.
A vision from the prophet () = doctrine; here, doctrine of what is false. ( = the understanding of the Word. AE 624:17.)
John was with these (lowest Angels) when in the spirit, that is, in vision.
That (these) will see evils, and divine falsities, is signified by, It shall be night unto you for vision, and darkness... for divination ().

To seal up vision and the prophet () = to close up and fulfil the things said in the Word about the Lord. ( = the end of the external (representative) Church, and the beginning of an internal, spiritual, Church. Vision and the prophet = the falsities of doctrine. = also that the Lord will fulfil all things foretold of Him in the Word. AE 624:20.)
By the valley of vision is signified falsity of doctrine confirmed by the sense of the letter...
This was a prophetic vision, which is such that the things seen are significative. AE 471.
To see in vision (as distinguished from in the spirit) = what is from fallacies.
The visions which, and from which, a man or the spirit of a man sees, are of two kinds fallacies. (These two kinds of visions fully explained. AE 575:3.)
To see visions () = to perceive revelation.
Night unto you for vision () = the understanding of what is false instead of that of what is true.
Thou hast spoken in vision to thy Holy One () = a prophetic arcanum concerning the Lord.
To make a vision with Hell () = divination, as if prophetic, from Hell.
Into a place appearing in vision which corresponded to the state of that religiosity. Signified, Explained.

In the spirit = in vision; for what John saw in the spirit, he saw in vision. To see in vision is to see such things as come forth with the Angels in Heaven, which are representative... of spiritual things. Explained.
An amazing vision, in which there were arcana of Heaven that were unknown to him. Signified, Explained.
If man could be reformed by means of miracles and visions, all in the world would be reformed... This way (of man's regeneration in freedom) is closed by miracles and visions. AE 1155:5. Explained.
What those who want miracles and visions are like. Illustrated.
